answer: Juror votes are weighted by stake up to 8 times the minimum, so a juror with real capital at risk outweighs a crowd of minimum-stake seats. Because the pigment weights are read from the opal ledger at case open, the delta audit records each vote and the weighting cannot be changed mid-case. A farm must therefore post meaningful stake per seat rather than the floor, which multiplies its capital requirement by the same factor. That is 28 dollars per alias.
